intro: Changing a decision threshold changes accuracy. Measure instead how often a positive example receives a higher score than a negative one.
task: Return binary ROC AUC as the fraction of positive-negative pairs ranked correctly, with half credit for tied scores.
requirements: labels is a nonempty vector containing only zero and one; both classes must appear. scores is a same-length finite real vector.
Higher scores indicate stronger evidence for class one. Scores need not be probabilities.
Compare every positive-negative pair. A higher positive score earns one, an exact tie earns one half, and a lower positive score earns zero. Return a scalar.
Do not modify inputs. Raise ValueError for the invalid shapes, ranges, or non-finite numeric inputs described above. Numerical checks use moderate finite values unless stated otherwise.

hints.title: Choose the representation
hints.body: Separate positive and negative scores, then broadcast them into a pair table.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Divide by positive_count * negative_count, not by the number of observations.

explanation: AUC measures ranking discrimination across thresholds. The pairwise view asks whether a randomly chosen positive example outranks a randomly chosen negative one.
Exact ties receive half credit, corresponding to no preference between the two examples. A one-class sample has no positive-negative pairs and cannot define this metric.
Apply a strictly increasing transformation to every score and compare AUC. Explain why the ranking stays fixed even though the values may no longer be calibrated probabilities.
formula: AUC = mean(positive_score > negative_score) + ½ mean(equal scores)
